children: , the social-media and AI company, hit a new distribution wall Monday after Amazon

blocked its Muse AI agent from shopping on the e-commerce giant's marketplace. Shares climbed nearly 7% to $711.62, based on the latest quoted price in the chart, sharpening the contrast between Meta's strong stock momentum and the commercial restrictions now confronting its agent strategy.

Muse is built to do more than answer questions. The agent can browse websites, fill out forms and move toward a purchase before asking users for final approval. Meta has paired the system with Stripe's Link infrastructure, including one-time-use payment cards, while saying Muse cannot access customer passwords or card information. That makes the Amazon decision important: an AI agent can be technically capable of completing transactions, but its usefulness still depends on whether major platforms allow it through the front door.

The valuation picture adds another layer. At $711.62, Meta trades roughly 16.7% below its GF Value estimate of $854.23. The gap suggests the shares remain below GuruFocus' estimate of fair value even after the latest rally. Consumer traction is encouragingBarron's reported that Muse topped free U.S. iPhone downloads for three straight daysbut downloads alone do not guarantee monetization. Amazon's block exposes the bigger issue: Meta can win users, build capable agents and create payment rails, yet third-party platform access may ultimately determine how much of that engagement becomes real transaction or subscription revenue.

title: Meta Jumps Nearly 7% as Amazon Blocks Muse From Shopping on Its Marketplace
